При движении намагниченного шарика внутр: When a magnetized ball moves inside a metal tube (in this experiment – aluminum), eddy currents arise in the tube walls, called Foucault currents. Due to these currents, a braking force acts on the ball, which is proportional to the velocity {0} of the ball's motion: {1}. The proportionality coefficient {2} in this formula depends on the tube parameters (its material and geometric dimensions) and the structure of the magnetic field created by the ball. This braking force phenomenon is often called magnetic viscosity. In this problem, you need to experimentally investigate this phenomenon.
